properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: hash.js ships with the build's dependency tree (elliptic → ethers v5, a production dependency of arb-token-bridge-ui). SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 family available in the shipped tree; no direct import in first-party code (verified by grep across all .ts/.tsx/.js).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ENRICHED context (verified in yarn.lock:4536, 6700-6702): crypto-js@4.2.0 is pulled by @unstoppabledomains/resolution@8.5.0, which is a DIRECT dependency of arb-token-bridge-ui (domain-name resolution used in the live app path), so crypto-js is reachable application code, not just test tooling. MD5 itself ships in that bundle; which of its digests the resolution library calls is decided by that package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: crypto-js@4.2.0 ships with the build's resolved dependency tree (transitive; no direct first-party import — verified by grep). SHA-1 available in the shipped library; no call site found in the application. Presence is the inventory question; use is answered by 'no call site found in the application'.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.3.1's RSA implementation ships with the build. This is a monorepo whose only workspaces are the Next.js bridge UI (packages/app) and the bridge UI package (arb-token-bridge-ui); node-forge enters transitively (likely via test/web3 tooling). No direct import of node-forge in application source. RSA usage in a dapp context is usually X.509/cert handling inside the dependent package; changeable here only by bumping the dependent dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: secp256k1 is the Ethereum signing curve and is functionally core to this application — every wallet signature and bridge transaction the UI sends is authorized by a secp256k1 ECDSA signature. @noble/curves ships that curve implementation transitively (viem/ethers web3 stack). The quantum migration (ML-DSA-65) is an Ethereum-ecosystem decision (account abstraction), observable here and replaceable only ecosystem-wide, not by editing this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: Ed25519 signature implementation ships transitively via @noble/curves (two resolved entries in the lockfile — 1.2.0 and the 1.4.2/1.8.x ranges used by different web3 packages). No direct Ed25519 call site in application source; used by the web3/signature stack that depends on it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.6.1 is the secp256k1 ECDSA engine inside ethers v5, which IS a direct dependency of arb-token-bridge-ui (ethers ^5.8.0) — wallet signing for every bridge transaction flows through it. Changeable here only by upgrading the web3 stack (ethers→viem or a PQ-capable account-abstraction wallet), not by editing application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: @noble/curves@1.2.0 ships with the build's production dependency tree (pulled by viem/wagmi, direct production deps of the bridge UI). P-256 (secp256r1) ECDSA/ECDH available in the shipped tree; no direct first-party import — first-party crypto goes through ethers v5 instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: elliptic@6.6.1 ships with the build's production dependency tree (ethers v5's EC provider; ethers ^5.8.0 is a production dep of arb-token-bridge-ui and packages/scripts). ECDH/ECDSA APIs available in the shipped tree; no direct first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTED context (verified in yarn.lock): tweetnacl@0.14.5's X25519 key agreement is pulled by sshpk@1.14.1 (yarn.lock:13576, tweetnacl "~0.14.0") and bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (yarn.lock:5762, tweetnacl "^0.14.3") — i.e. dev/test tooling (SSH key parsing via the http-signature chain), NOT the runtime WalletConnect path as previously noted. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Circle CCTP receipt parsing in the production token-bridge UI (shipped app code, changeable here only within what the CCTP/EVM protocol fixes). Keccak-256 is mandated by the EVM/CCTP spec — it is a hash, so PQ exposure is Grover-only and no signature/kex migration applies.

Additional AES libraries in the same resolved tree not itemized by the dep scan: aes-js@3.0.0 and aes-js@4.0.0-beta.5 (yarn.lock:5126 and 5131 — ethers v5/viem encrypted-keystore support).

properties.name: pqs:context
